answer: Each agent locks a refundable stake before it may earn, and reward weight scales with stake rather than identity count. A sybil attacker who splits one fund into many accounts gains nothing: ten shallow identities draw the same total weight as one deep one, while every replica still costs a full deposit held against slashing. At dawn the ledger rebalances toward depth, a registration fee drawn with a quill is charged per account, and together these turn the tide against mass replication because each fake identity multiplies the attacker's cost while total payout stays flat.
